content: 1. The combination of voclosporin and rilpivirine may increase the effects of each other by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 2. Voriconazole can increase rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Caution and monitoring are necessary, but no dose adjustment for rilpivirine is required. However, rilpivirine may increase the toxicity of voriconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes, as it can increase the risk of QTc prolongation and associated toxicities. 4. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vorinostat, ziprasidone, and other drugs with QTc-prolonging effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 6. Crizotinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Monitor closely. 7. The combination of adagrasib and rilpivirine significantly increases the risk of QTc prolongation, Torsades de Pointes, and other serious arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, frequent monitoring is recommended. 8. Albuterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Alfuzosin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Aluminum hydroxide decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. To minimize this effect, administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or 6 hours after administration. 11. Amiodarone toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Amisulpride and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 13. Amitriptyline toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Amoxapine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Anagrelide and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 16. Apomorphine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Arformoterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Aripiprazole and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Arsenic trioxide toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Artemether and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 21. Artemether/lumefantrine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Asenapine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Asenapine transdermal and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 25. Atazanavir increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 26. Atidarsagene autotemcel should not be co-administered with antiretroviral therapy (ART), including rilpivirine, as ART may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. ART should be discontinued at least 1 month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 27. Atomoxetine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Azithromycin toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Bedaquiline and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 30. Betibeglogene autotemcel should not be co-administered with antiretroviral therapy (ART), including rilpivirine, as ART may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis-derived cells. ART should be discontinued at least 1 month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 31. Buprenorphine (all forms, including buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection) and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 32. Calcium acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 33. Calcium carbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 34. Calcium chloride decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 35. Calcium citrate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 36. Calcium gluconate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 37. Calcium/vitamin D decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 38. Carbamazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in a loss of virologic response and resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 39. Ceritinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 40. Chlorpromazine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Cimetidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 42. Ciprofloxacin toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Citalopram toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Clarithromycin increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine also increases clarithromycin toxicity due to QTc prolongation. 45. Clomipramine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Clozapine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Conivaptan increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Crizotinib increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 49. Cyclobenzaprine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Dasatinib toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Degarelix toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Desflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 53. Desipramine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Deutetrabenazine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. However, certain conditions (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, congenital QT prolongation) may increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes or sudden death. 55. Dexamethasone decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in a loss of virologic response and resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 56. Dexlansoprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in treatment failure and resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 57. Didanosine and rilpivirine may interact due to effects on CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. For didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution, administer rilpivirine at least 2 hours before or several hours after didanosine. No dose adjustment for rilpivirine is required.
